summary: This note covers the 1827 State of the Union Address, written and delivered by President John Quincy Adams on Tuesday, December 4, 1827. The address was given to both chambers of Congress, the House of Representatives and the Senate, and was addressed to the 20th United States Congress. Adams opens by noting that a full revolution of the seasons had passed since Congress last met to act on the nation's common interests.
one_line: John Quincy Adams's December 4, 1827 State of the Union Address to the 20th United States Congress.
key_facts: The 1827 State of the Union Address was written by John Quincy Adams.
John Quincy Adams was the sixth President of the United States.
The 1827 State of the Union Address was given on Tuesday, December 4, 1827.
The 1827 State of the Union Address was given to the United States House of Representatives and United States Senate.
The 1827 State of the Union Address was given to the 20th United States Congress.

John Quincy Adams opened the 1827 State of the Union Address by saying, "A revolution of the seasons has nearly been completed since the representatives of the people and States of this Union were last assembled at this place to deliberate and to act upon the common important interests of their constituents."
